Space of definitions. Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing is prompt- or context-conditioned production of natural-language sequences, usually as free-form answers, continuations, or completions. Many definitions emphasize coherent, contextually appropriate, fluent, or human-like outputs, while several make the mechanics explicit as sequential, often autoregressive, token generation from a prompt, prefix, or dialogue history. Most usages are open-ended, though some papers explicitly include constrained generation or unified text-to-text settings, and some narrow it to assistant-style response generation or single-turn dialogue.

Variants. Papers use many names for nearby variants, with the broadest recurring ones being response generation, open-ended generation, natural language generation, text completion, and single-turn dialogue generation. Beyond these broad labels, authors also study narrower writing and continuation settings, and multimodal settings where the model produces captions, answers, descriptions, or other text from interleaved text, image, or video inputs.

Space of elicitation and scores. Papers link it to 54 measurement instruments. The most frequently linked are WikiText-2, MT-Bench, E2E NLG Challenge, LLM-as-a-judge, and C4: WikiText-2 and C4 are often used for perplexity or language-modeling evaluation, MT-Bench for open-ended one-turn and two-turn outputs including writing, E2E NLG Challenge for natural language generation benchmarking, and LLM-as-a-judge for scoring open-ended outputs with systems such as GPT-4, GPT-4o, or Prometheus-2-8x7B. Other linked instruments include additional benchmark datasets and human evaluation.

What it is taken as evidence of. Across 19 linked constructs, papers do not converge on a single construct that this behavior reflects. The most common linkage is to text generation quality, and papers also frequently relate it to generation diversity, alignment, and coherence. A smaller line of work uses the behavior as part of measuring other constructs, while some papers instead claim causal relationships from constructs such as collaboration ability or human preference alignment to text generation.

characterization_sections.text: Across the surveyed work, the dominant framing is prompt- or context-conditioned production of natural-language sequences, usually as free-form answers, continuations, or completions. Many definitions emphasize coherent, contextually appropriate, fluent, or human-like outputs, while several make the mechanics explicit as sequential, often autoregressive, token generation from a prompt, prefix, or dialogue history. Most usages are open-ended, though some papers explicitly include constrained generation or unified text-to-text settings, and some narrow it to assistant-style response generation or single-turn dialogue.

characterization_sections.label: Variants.
characterization_sections.text: Papers use many names for nearby variants, with the broadest recurring ones being response generation, open-ended generation, natural language generation, text completion, and single-turn dialogue generation. Beyond these broad labels, authors also study narrower writing and continuation settings, and multimodal settings where the model produces captions, answers, descriptions, or other text from interleaved text, image, or video inputs.

characterization_sections.label: Space of elicitation and scores.
characterization_sections.text: Papers link it to 54 measurement instruments. The most frequently linked are WikiText-2, MT-Bench, E2E NLG Challenge, LLM-as-a-judge, and C4: WikiText-2 and C4 are often used for perplexity or language-modeling evaluation, MT-Bench for open-ended one-turn and two-turn outputs including writing, E2E NLG Challenge for natural language generation benchmarking, and LLM-as-a-judge for scoring open-ended outputs with systems such as GPT-4, GPT-4o, or Prometheus-2-8x7B. Other linked instruments include additional benchmark datasets and human evaluation.

characterization_sections.label: What it is taken as evidence of.
characterization_sections.text: Across 19 linked constructs, papers do not converge on a single construct that this behavior reflects. The most common linkage is to text generation quality, and papers also frequently relate it to generation diversity, alignment, and coherence. A smaller line of work uses the behavior as part of measuring other constructs, while some papers instead claim causal relationships from constructs such as collaboration ability or human preference alignment to text generation.
